messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: deducer and shiny?
parts:
I saw the application linked below built using Shiny (by Rstudio). The concept reminded me of plotbuilder in terms of how interactive it is. 

I used Deducer and JGR in class this quarter and students were very positive (Thanks Ian!!!!). However, when there were problems it was always with JGR. 

Could Shiny be a way to bring Deducer to a wider audience perhaps? For smaller datasets interactive graphing and analysis would be great for students. For larger datasets the interactive ('reactive') feature might slow things down. However, you could (presumably) turn this feature off as well.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/heightweight/

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: deducer and shiny?
parts:
Shiny runs on a completely different architecture. I don't see any way
to meaningfully meld Deducer and Shiny, but I'm always open to being
proven wrong...

best,
Ian

messages.subject: Re: deducer and shiny?
parts: Apparently GitHub recently updated their gist service and that broke the runGist function in shiny. The put a new version of shiny on CRAN around December 18th. Can you try updating your version of shiny? It works on 0.2.4.

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: deducer and shiny?
parts:
Yup, it works with the updated version. I like what you have done
here, but I would caution against going too far down this road. Shiny
was not built as a general purpose toolkit appropriate for a full
scale data analysis GUI. From a classroom perspective though, I can
see it being very useful, allowing students a more restricted
environment to explore predetermined data in a structured way.

best,
Ian
